query: The (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 high-entropy alloy is a solid refrigeration working medium that exhibits a large caloric response under applied-field and pressure-field operation but has poor load-bearing integrity and tends to crack. What single intervention could increase its integrity while preserving caloric performance in these operating regimes? State one hypothesis specifying the intervention, its proposed mechanism, predicted integrity and caloric outcomes relative to the unchanged alloy, applicable field, pressure, temperature, and loading boundaries, supporting prior evidence, and a controlled experiment with explicit results that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Creating a hierarchical microstructure with a combination of coarse and fine grains in the (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 high-entropy alloy will increase its load-bearing integrity while preserving its caloric performance under applied-field and pressure-field operation.
generation.intervention: Creating a hierarchical microstructure with a combination of coarse and fine grains
generation.mechanism: The combination of coarse and fine grains will enhance the strength and toughness of the alloy, allowing it to withstand higher loads and stresses while maintaining its caloric performance.
generation.predicted_outcome: Increased load-bearing integrity and preserved caloric performance
generation.baseline: The current (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 high-entropy alloy with poor load-bearing integrity and tendency to crack
generation.boundary: The alloy will be operated under applied-field and pressure-field conditions, with temperatures not exceeding the limits of the alloy's stability
generation.uncertainty: The exact extent of the improvement in load-bearing integrity and the potential effects on caloric performance are uncertain and require further experimentation

falsification_experiment.design: A controlled experiment comparing the mechanical properties and caloric performance of the (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 high-entropy alloy with a hierarchical microstructure to those of the baseline alloy.
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the hierarchical microstructure does not result in a significant improvement in load-bearing integrity or a preservation of caloric performance, the hypothesis is falsified.

cited_evidence.text: However, there is also a question of the role of high configurational entropy in these materials with respect to properties, particularly how such high-entropy alloys compare with other equiatomic multi-element systems. Here we examine a variant of the single-phase CrMnFeCoNi high-entropy alloy in which two of the elements have been removed. The resulting CrCoNi alloy, an equiatomic ‘medium-entropy alloy' (MEA), has a single-phase, fcc crystal structure, whose uniaxial tensile properties have recently been reported. The experimental results (X-ray diffraction and backscattered electron, BSE, images) are consistent with the CrCoNi ternary phase diagrams, which indicate that the equiatomic composition is a single-phase solid solution at elevated temperatures. (XRD and BSE analyses of the five-component CrMnFeCoNi alloy after casting and homogenization showed that it too is single-phase fcc and remains so after recrystallization when examined by transmission electron microscopy. Such damage-tolerant properties of the CrCoNi medium-entropy alloy are literally unprecedented for mechanical behaviour at cryogenic temperatures. For a material with a tensile strength of 1.3 GPa to display ductilities (failure strains) of 90%, and ‘valid' crack-growth fracture toughnesses that exceeds 430 MPa m1/2, all at liquid-nitrogen temperatures, is exceptional and clearly exceed the excellent cryogenic properties of our previously reported CrMnFeCoNi high-entropy alloy. Its ductility compares favourably to high-Mn twinning-induced plasticity steels and strength and toughness are comparable to the very best cryogenic steels, for example, certain austenitic stainless steels and high-Ni steels; in addition, the strength, ductility and toughness of the CrCoNi alloy exceed the properties of all medium- and high-entropy alloys reported to date (Fig. 4). Moreover, with a uniformly fine grain size, it is eminently feasible that the strength, ductility and toughness properties of this CrCoNi alloy may further improve.
